topic: The Geometry of Light: Sphere Surface Area and Its Projected Shadow
target_audience: High school geometry or physics students

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisites (1 minute)
lecture_lines: A circle has an area of pi r squared.
A sphere is a three-dimensional curved surface.
Parallel light rays create a circular shadow.
animations: Fade in a sphere labeled 'S' in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Conceptualizing the Sphere Surface (1.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: The sphere surface area formula is 4 pi r squared.
The surface covers exactly four flat circles.
Each circle has the sphere's radius.
Total area is four times pi r squared.
animations: Show a sphere surface moving, color #00FFFF.
Highlight a point 'P' on the surface in #FF0000.

sections.title: The Projection Logic (1.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: Compare 3D surface area to 2D shadow area.
Shadows capture only the sphere's cross-section.
Spinning the sphere keeps the shadow circular.
Shadow area is always pi r squared.
Surface area is four times the shadow area.
animations: Draw ray from center 'O' through 'P' in #00FF00.
Show intersection point 'P_prime' on a plane in #FFCC00.

sections.title: Summary & Application (1 minute)
lecture_lines: The sphere's surface is 4 times its shadow.
This ratio is critical for heat and light.
animations: Flash the projection process for points in #00FF00.
Final fade to black with 'Conclusion' in #FFFFFF.
